name: BASS / BASS-II
objective: Investigate solid-fuel ignition, spread and extinction under controlled low-speed flow.
fuels: Plastic films, rods and composite fabric; exact materials and sizes are test-specific.
geometry: Small solid samples in a flow duct; keep rods, films and fabrics distinct.
hardware: BASS-II flow duct in the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox; video camera with data overlay and a 35-mm still camera. Apparatus details are campaign-specific.
measurements: For BASS-II, CSA-CP provided oxygen and carbon monoxide readings; a Carbon Dioxide Monitor measured carbon dioxide before and after tests. The report describes comparison with ISS Major Constituents Analyzer oxygen readings.
summary: Solid-material research relevant to material screening, flame spread and extinction questions.
limitation: Small samples and a specific duct do not establish whole-cabin behavior. Measurements and sensors are not interchangeable across tests.
interpretation: Use this investigation to identify relevant solid-material experiments; assess scale, geometry and atmospheric mismatches before transferring findings.
sourceLabel: BASS-II Summary Report, apparatus and test matrices
evidenceLevel: Curated test records and publication findings
scopeNotes: BASS and BASS-II are grouped for discovery. The sensor description above is specifically supported by the BASS-II report; it is not a universal specification for all BASS campaigns.

name: Saffire
objective: Study larger spacecraft fires and their behavior in uncrewed cargo vehicles.
fuels: Solid samples; material, sample size and configuration vary by flight and test.
geometry: Larger samples than glovebox-scale tests; consult each run for dimensions and confinement.
hardware: Saffire Flow Unit inside uncrewed Cygnus spacecraft; hardware and diagnostics vary by flight.
measurements: Flame-spread and video observations. The Saffire VI publication discusses heat release, spacecraft temperature and carbon dioxide/carbon monoxide; IV-VI apparatus descriptions include inlet/outlet gas sensing. Check each flight before comparing sensors.
summary: A spacecraft-scale research context for flame spread and fire-safety questions.
limitation: Scale, atmosphere and materials can change together. A result from one flight is not a controlled comparison with another by default.
interpretation: Use spacecraft-scale evidence alongside small-sample studies, keeping differences visible rather than pooling their outcomes.
sourceLabel: NASA overview, Saffire paragraph and linked publications
evidenceLevel: Curated test records and publication findings
scopeNotes: The investigation group spans multiple flights. A sensor configuration or finding from IV-VI is not automatically a specification or outcome for I-III.

name: SAME / SAME-R
objective: Characterize spacecraft-material smoke and assess smoke-detector response in reduced gravity.
fuels: Smoke generated from spacecraft materials; the overview lists Teflon, Kapton, cellulose and silicone rubber.
geometry: Smoke-generation and aerosol-sampling experiment; not a solid flame-spread geometry.
hardware: Smoke-generation, aerosol measurement and detector-test apparatus; configurations need the original investigation documentation.
measurements: Aerosol number, size and mass-related measurements, plus ionization and photoelectric detector evaluation. NASA reports material-dependent smoke-size distributions; these aggregate results are not individual detector-performance records.
summary: Detection-focused research that connects smoke properties to detector evaluation.
limitation: No numerical SAME detector-performance time series are curated here. The NASA document includes aggregate smoke-property results; source-table smoke-generation conditions do not establish alarm sensitivity, false-alarm rate or timing for a chosen habitat.
interpretation: Relevant to detector research and data collection; this overview cannot establish alarm performance for a selected habitat.
sourceLabel: NASA SAME / SAME-R document, PDF pages 1–2 and reflight section
evidenceLevel: Published smoke-property findings, source metadata and smoke-generation conditions; no validated detector-performance model
scopeNotes: The original NASA document includes results as well as objectives. Aggregate publication findings are kept separate from individual test rows and detector validation.
SAME-R has its own profile. Its modified hardware and materials are not assumed equivalent to the original SAME configuration.
PSI source-table metadata remains separate from curated solid-fuel outcome rows. Smoke generation settings do not become detector response or alarm-performance measurements.

name: FLEX / FLEX-2
objective: Examine droplet burning, extinction, suppressant effects and fuel-mixture behavior.
fuels: Liquid-fuel droplets; mixtures and experimental conditions vary by investigation.
geometry: Droplet combustion rather than solid sheets, fabrics or panels.
hardware: Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) inside the Combustion Integrated Rack in the ISS Destiny module.
measurements: Droplet/flame observations and extinction-related measurements. The report documents hardware, diagnostic equipment, procedures and analysis; instrument specifications must be checked in the original report.
summary: Liquid-droplet evidence for combustion and extinction mechanisms.
limitation: Droplet behavior does not establish solid-material flammability. Visible-flame disappearance alone does not prove all combustion has ended.
interpretation: Use as mechanistic evidence for suppression questions, clearly separated from a solid-material or cabin outcome.
evidenceLevel: Publication-level mechanisms; no curated numerical test rows
scopeNotes: The library group includes FLEX/FLEX-2, but the linked numerical publication findings here cite the FLEX report covering March 2009-December 2011. No FLEX or FLEX-2 individual test table has been imported into this corpus.

name: ACME
objective: Study gaseous-flame behavior to improve combustion efficiency and reduce pollutants; Burning Rate Emulator addresses materials flammability and spacecraft fire-prevention questions.
fuels: Gaseous fuels in several distinct investigations.
geometry: Gas-flame configurations vary across the ACME investigations.
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack with modular investigation hardware.
measurements: Flame/soot and investigation-specific combustion measurements; one common sensor specification is not asserted.
summary: Gas-flame mechanisms relevant to combustion research and some prevention questions.
limitation: A gas-flame mechanism or electrical-field analogy is not a direct solid-material measurement at lunar or Martian gravity.
interpretation: Keep gas-flame evidence in a mechanistic category when interpreting material-selection questions.
sourceLabel: NASA Science ACME mission: investigations and applications
evidenceLevel: Publication-level mechanisms; no curated numerical test rows
scopeNotes: ACME contains distinct investigations with different objectives. Burning Rate Emulator is the spacecraft-fire-prevention component; the other investigations primarily address terrestrial combustion. Keep those application scopes separate.

name: SoFIE-GEL
objective: Investigate solid-flame growth and extinction with controlled heating and atmosphere.
fuels: PMMA sphere in the GEL investigation; this does not describe every SoFIE investigation.
geometry: Thick spherical solid fuel; different from a flat fabric or panel.
hardware: SoFIE investigation in the Combustion Integrated Rack.
measurements: Growth/extinction characteristics, flame shape and dimensions; source describes comparison with a numerical model.
summary: A controlled solid-fuel study linking atmosphere, airflow and heating to growth/extinction research.
limitation: The investigation overview is not a numerical results table. No SoFIE-GEL test rows are curated in this app.
interpretation: Relevant to early growth/extinction research; do not infer a threshold for a different shape or habitat from the overview.
sourceLabel: NASA Science, objectives and experiment description
evidenceLevel: Objectives/design overview and related publication context
scopeNotes: This profile describes SoFIE-GEL. The linked 2020 SoFIE project findings are broader parent-program context, not numerical results from GEL.

name: LUCI
objective: Investigate solid-material burning under simulated lunar gravity.
fuels: SIBAL fabric and PMMA rod in the curated records.
geometry: Different sample geometries on a spinning sounding-rocket platform.
hardware: Spinning sounding rocket; centrifugal acceleration creates the gravity analogue.
measurements: Reported flame-spread observations; limited duration and Coriolis effects remain relevant.
summary: A limited partial-gravity analogue, kept distinct from orbital and Moon-surface measurements.
limitation: Two curated burns are not a general lunar habitat dataset. These are simulated lunar-gravity results, not measurements on the Moon.
interpretation: A closer gravity analogy can inform research questions while platform, duration and geometry mismatches remain explicit.
sourceLabel: LUCI publication; see the page-linked curated burn records
scopeNotes: The two curated runs use simulated lunar acceleration in a rotating rocket. They are not Moon-surface measurements, and initial oxygen values do not describe the complete burn history.

name: SPICE
objective: Study how coflow and burner size change non-buoyant gas-jet smoke points and luminous flame length.
fuels: Gaseous jet fuels; fuel-specific composition must be read from each source test.
geometry: Laminar round-jet diffusion flame surrounded by an oxidizer coflow.
hardware: SPICE coflow burner hardware in the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox.
measurements: Smoke-point onset, flame shape and length; source describes imaging and temperature-field studies.
summary: Gas-flame soot and radiation research that supports combustion-model questions.
limitation: Smoke-point behavior is not a smoke-detector sensitivity test or a solid-material flammability limit. No individual SPICE rows are imported here.
interpretation: Use soot/flow relationships to choose model inputs; validate separately for cabin materials and ventilation.
evidenceLevel: Source-linked investigation metadata and publication context; no imported individual test rows
scopeNotes: NASA PSI catalog entry PSI-107 (DOI 10.60555/9kbh-e962) provides a separate data-access route. This profile does not imply that its complete files have been imported.

name: SLICE
objective: Study flame-base structure and liftoff limits to test non-premixed combustion models.
fuels: Methane, ethylene and selected nitrogen-diluted mixtures burning in a coflow of air.
geometry: Attached and lifted coflow diffusion flames; burner diameter is a studied variable.
hardware: SPICE-derived burner hardware in the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox; procedures differ from SPICE.
measurements: Still/video observations of flame structure and base position during changes in airflow.
summary: Flame stabilization research linking imaging and detailed numerical combustion models.
limitation: The source describes objectives and proposed methods. Liftoff of a gas flame is not a measured solid-fuel extinction threshold.
interpretation: Use as mechanistic context for ventilation/flame-stability questions, with configuration differences visible.
evidenceLevel: Source-linked investigation metadata and publication context; no imported individual test rows
scopeNotes: SLICE is a precursor to ACME CLD Flame, not an interchangeable campaign. Shared hardware does not imply equivalent tests.

name: CFI — Cool Flame Investigation
objective: Study n-dodecane droplet combustion, helium dilution, soot formation and relationships among size, pressure and extinction.
fuels: n-dodecane, n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures and farnesane described in PSI metadata.
hardware: Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus within the ISS Combustion Integrated Rack.
measurements: Black-and-white droplet imaging, UV OH* / flame-size imaging, and narrow-/wide-band radiometry.
summary: Liquid-droplet cool-flame research, distinct from original FLEX and gaseous CFI-G.
limitation: PSI objectives and approach give inconsistent pressure-range descriptions. No reconciled flight envelope or individual CFI outcome table is asserted here.
interpretation: Plan diagnostics that can distinguish hot-flame disappearance from continuing low-temperature chemistry.
evidenceLevel: Source-linked investigation metadata and publication context; no imported individual test rows
scopeNotes: PSI-39 objective and approach pressure ranges differ; consult original test tables before selecting an experimental envelope.
The supplementary 2014 concept-review excerpt is historical design context. Its illustrated FLEX tests are not relabelled as CFI flight results.

name: CFI-G — Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
objective: Observe quasi-steady spherical cool diffusion flames on porous burners to study low-temperature chemistry.
fuels: Propane, n-butane and n-pentane with varied reactant dilutions in the PSI objectives; normal and inverse flame configurations.
geometry: Normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames on a porous burner.
hardware: ACME hardware in the ISS Combustion Integrated Rack, with intensified imaging and thermal measurements.
measurements: Cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes and thermocouples in PSI metadata; the NTRS presentation reports a cool-flame observation.
summary: Gas-fueled cool-flame observations and chemistry-model research for cleaner combustion.
limitation: Reported observations do not supply a complete numerical test table, suppression recipe or solid-material fire limit.
interpretation: Treat faint emissions and continuing chemistry as a diagnostics/modeling question; do not equate visual darkness with a safe condition.
sourceLabel: NASA ACME presentation, CFI-G selected finding
evidenceLevel: Source-linked investigation metadata and publication context; no imported individual test rows
scopeNotes: CFI-G burns gaseous fuels on a porous burner; CFI studies liquid droplets. Neither is a controlled comparison with a habitat fire.

name: E-FIELD Flames
objective: Understand flame ion production and electric-field control of non-premixed gas flames.
fuels: Gas-fueled flames, with or without coflow; source-specific fuel compositions remain test-level information.
geometry: Jet or coflow diffusion flame between a burner and downstream mesh electrode.
hardware: ACME Combustion Integrated Rack with burner, mesh electrode and high-voltage field.
measurements: Electric field, ion current and flame response, including structure, soot, temperature and stability.
summary: Electrical flame-control research aimed primarily at terrestrial combustion efficiency and emissions.
limitation: NASA states this research is not conducted for a space application. It is not demonstrated spacecraft fire-suppression equipment.
interpretation: Identify mechanisms and diagnostic signals for research; hardware safety and effectiveness require independent engineering tests.
evidenceLevel: Source-linked investigation metadata and publication context; no imported individual test rows
scopeNotes: The prevention tag describes fundamental combustion-control relevance, not a validated crew fire-control procedure.

name: FLEX-2
objective: Study liquid-droplet fuel mixtures, sub-buoyant flows and droplet interactions to improve combustion models.
fuels: Pure, bi-component and surrogate liquid fuels; fuel composition is campaign/test-specific.
geometry: Single droplets or binary arrays, including fiber-supported droplets and controlled relative flow.
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack and Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus; source-specific fiber, deployment and ignition configurations.
measurements: Recorded droplet burning and extinction behavior, including flow and droplet-interaction cases.
summary: A distinct droplet-modeling investigation with mixtures and interactions beyond the original FLEX focus.
limitation: The combined FLEX overview remains for discovery. Original FLEX report findings are not assigned to FLEX-2 by default; source-table parameters are not automatically burn-outcome labels.
interpretation: Compare mixture and geometry explicitly before using this mechanistic work to guide a fire-safety research question.
evidenceLevel: Source-linked investigation metadata and publication context; no imported individual test rows
scopeNotes: Separate FLEX-2 profile prevents its objectives being confused with findings from the original FLEX report. No original FLEX rows or findings are duplicated here.

name: SAME-R
objective: Quantify low-gravity smoke-particle sizes and relate distributions to smoke generation and transport.
fuels: Spacecraft smoke-source materials; SAME-R introduced Pyrell foam and changed conditions relative to SAME.
geometry: Smoke generation, transport, aging and aerosol sampling; not flame-spread geometry.
hardware: Modified SAME hardware, thermal precipitators and M-pass diagnostics in the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox.
measurements: Particle-size-distribution moments, microscopy and comparison with ground reference measurements.
summary: A distinct smoke-measurement reflight with modified materials, conditions and diagnostics.
limitation: The PSI catalog total and smoke-generation condition table do not establish detector alarm performance. Imported source metadata must retain row type, original units and missing cells.
interpretation: Use source-specific aerosol distributions and calibration to formulate detector validation rather than infer performance from flame outcomes.
evidenceLevel: PSI metadata and aggregate reported test count; detector-performance validation remains separate
scopeNotes: SAME-R is related to SAME but includes hardware and protocol changes. The reported total number of test points is an aggregate catalog statement, not that many imported rows.

name: FM² — Flammability of Materials on the Moon
objective: Plan lunar-surface observations of solid flame spread and compare material-screening behavior across gravity.
fuels: Four solid samples in the NASA hardware description; exact flight material selection requires its latest configuration record.
geometry: Individual samples burned in a sealed, autonomously controlled chamber.
hardware: Self-contained FM² lunar experiment chamber, gas supply, cameras and onboard sensors.
measurements: Planned flame size, intensity, color and spread-rate imaging; fuel/flame temperature, oxygen and carbon dioxide sensing.
summary: A lunar-surface research design that addresses a gap beyond simulated partial gravity.
limitation: The cited objectives and hardware description do not establish completed lunar measurements. No Moon-surface result rows are imported here.
interpretation: Keep planned lunar evidence separate from LUCI simulated-lunar results and from Earth/ISS comparisons.

evidenceLevel: Source-linked investigation metadata and publication context; no imported individual test rows
